title: Inherited Weights: Measuring the Tokenization Premium and the Sovereignty Cost of Language Models for the Global South
abstract: arXiv:2611.13441v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Most language models deployed outside the United States and China are fine-tuned descendants of a small number of pretrained families. We argue that fine-tuning leaves the decisive properties of a model inherited from its base: vocabulary, knowledge, cultural alignment, memorized data and license. We contribute (i) an updated, reproducible measurement of the tokenization premium across 31 languages and 7 tokenizers released in 2023-2024, on 27 articles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, with explicit correction for unknown-token collapse. Premiums reach 10x for Amharic in older tokenizers and remain at 6.8x in the newest commercial one; Indigenous South American languages pay between 1.6x and 2.7x under global tokenizers. A vocabulary built from Portuguese lowers the premium for 11 of 13 Latin-script Global South languages relative to every global tokenizer tested, by about 24% for Guarani and Quechua. translated_title: 继承的权重：测量全球南方语言模型的分词溢价与主权成本
translated_abstract: 在美国和中国之外部署的大多数语言模型，都是由少数预训练模型家族微调而来的后代。我们认为，微调使得模型的决定性属性——词表、知识、文化对齐、被记忆的数据以及许可证——都从其基础模型继承而来。我们的贡献包括：(i) 对分词溢价的更新且可复现的测量，涵盖31种语言和2023-2024年发布的7个分词器，基于《世界人权宣言》的27条条文，并对未知词元坍缩进行了显性校正。较旧分词器中阿姆哈拉语的溢价高达10倍，在最新的商业分词器中仍为6.8倍；南美洲原住民语言在全球分词器下需支付1.6倍至2.7倍的溢价。由葡萄牙语构建的词表，相对于所有被测试的全球分词器，可降低13种拉丁字母书写的全球南方语言中11种的溢价，其中瓜拉尼语和克丘亚语约降低24%。(ii) 一套包含八项测试的基准……（摘要原文在此处被截断）
tldr: 论文指出微调模型会从基础模型继承词表、知识、文化对齐、数据与许可证等决定性属性，并测量出全球南方语言承受最高达10倍的分词溢价，证明构建本地化词表可将该溢价显著降低约24%，从而揭示了大语言模型给全球南方带来的主权成本。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that fine-tuned models inherit decisive properties—vocabulary, knowledge, cultural alignment, memorized data, and license—from their base models, and measures a tokenization premium of up to 10x for Global South languages, demonstrating that locally built vocabularies can reduce this premium by about 24% and thus quantifying the sovereignty cost of language models for the Global South.
